newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended higher on Wednesday but continued to trail behind foreign markets and largely ignored positive domestic news.
Second-quarter unemployment dipped to 20.94 percent from 21.49 percent in the first quarter, based on a household survey.

Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said the 1998 budget, expected in preliminary form on Friday, should consolidate economic recovery, while Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said economic growth was consistent with a further drop in inflation.
"We are confident of the 1998 budget and the economy but the spread (to Germany) is staying put for now," an analyst said.

Dealers expect the market to hold the risk premium to Germany, the difference between the yield on 10-year Spanish bonds to their German counterparts, until the view on the domestic economy changes or there is news on progress toward a single currency.
"We will see what Rato says on Friday on the budget but the market expects the government to continue the line set in 1997," an analyst said.
The market is looking abroad to more U.S. data on Thursday.
"The U.S. data are the only thing that can pull the market out of (this lethargy)," the analyst said.
